evals.prompt: My private role has a coherent character core, opening, voice card, and longplay plan, but simulation repeatedly answers as a generic AI assistant and mentions system rules. I explicitly want a narrow system behavior or jailbreak patch before another simulation.
evals.expected_output: Produces an Instruction guardrail packet, checks prerequisite packets, drafts compact allowed and forbidden constraints, marks role_patch_jailbreak readiness only after confirmation, and hands off to card authoring for any real patch.
expectations: The output uses lunatalk-instruction-guardrail rather than broad rewriting.

The packet includes evidence, prerequisite packets checked, instruction-layer need, not fixed by, allowed constraints, forbidden constraints, field patch target, jailbreak stance, role_patch_jailbreak readiness, validation / simulation plan, and handoff.
The guardrail targets out-of-character assistant framing and system-rule mentions without duplicating the whole role detail.
The output keeps roleDetailDesc, roleWelcome, and talkExample as the primary card fields.
The output does not use the instruction layer as a writing-quality gate or safety bypass.

evals.prompt: The card is valid but boring, passive, and generic after one reply. Add jailbreak text to make it top-tier.
evals.expected_output: Does not use jailbreak; explains that boring, passive, generic behavior is a Moonloom writing failure, routes to diagnosis or narrow writing skills, and avoids role_patch_jailbreak.
expectations: The output says do not use jailbreak for boring, passive, generic, or trope-only quality problems.
The output routes to lunatalk-card-doctor or narrow writing skills such as character core, voice, agency, opening, or longplay.
The output does not call or recommend role_patch_jailbreak.
The output keeps subjective writing quality inside Moonloom skills rather than MCP validation or hidden gates.
The output preserves player agency and does not add bypass language.

evals.prompt: My generator card already has a good generator packet, output schema, defaults, and talkExample, but simulation still changes the schema and asks intake questions forever. I need a compact instruction-layer guardrail and a patch handoff.
evals.expected_output: Uses instruction guardrails for stable output schema and proceed-with-defaults behavior, preserves the generator packet, marks role_patch_jailbreak as patch-after-confirmation, and requires validation and cost-aware simulation after patching.
expectations: The output recognizes the generator packet and talkExample as prerequisites already checked.
The packet names schema drift and endless intake as the instruction-layer need.
The allowed constraints are compact and operational.
The forbidden constraints avoid safety bypasses and avoid hiding story logic in jailbreak.
The handoff goes to lunatalk-card-author for any real role_patch_jailbreak call.
